title: Finite geometric exchange and projection commute with shifts
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient datum of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ has characteristic $p$, $\ell\ne p$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, $n\ge1$, and $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. All schemes below are separated and of finite type over $k$. Work on their small pro-etale sites with bounded constructible constant-$A$ module complexes of finite Tor amplitude, denoted $D^b_{ctf}(-,A)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Use the geometric operations and specified constructible exceptional adjunctions of [def-trf-admissibility], and the external tensor product and canonical comparisons of [def-sf-kv-maps] specialized to $A$.

Let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y'\to Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-morphisms, and let $X'=X\times_Y Y'$ with projections $f':X'\to Y'$ and $g':X'\to X$. Use the exchange and projection transformations whose chosen-compactification formulas are those of [def-exchange-projection]; on the bounded etale-origin domain they are independent of the compactification by [fix-lem-exchanges](4) and [fix-prop-projection-formula] (compatibility with the compactification comparisons):
$$\operatorname{Ex}_{!,K}:Lg^*Rf_!K\longrightarrow Rf'_!Lg'^*K,\qquad
\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}:Rf_!K\otimes_A^L L\longrightarrow Rf_!(K\otimes_A^L Lf^*L),$$
for $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ and $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$. Give pullback, tensor and compact support their canonical derived integer-shift comparisons, including the signed total-tensor comparisons in either tensor input. The exchange commutes with shifting $K$, and the projection transformation commutes separately with shifting $K$ and with shifting $L$. Precisely, for each of these three one-variable transformations $\tau:\Phi\to\Psi$, every integer $m$, and every input $M$, the equality
$$\chi_{\Psi,m,M}\circ\tau_{M[m]}=\tau_M[m]\circ\chi_{\Phi,m,M}$$
holds, where $\chi_{F,m,M}:F(M[m])\xrightarrow{\sim}F(M)[m]$ is the indicated canonical composite shift. These are the actual geometric maps. Their inverses, wherever the maps are isomorphisms, satisfy the same equation with source and target reversed.

source.place: Paragraph 4: both sides of alpha are exact in each coefficient, so triangle two-out-of-three applies; retained Step 9, geometric exchange/projection shift check; the precise compatibility assertion is extracted from the retained stage-1 argument, rather than quoted as a separate theorem of the source.

proof.text: Work first with a chosen compactification $c=(j,p)$ and its base change. All calculations take place in the ambient constant-$A$ module derived categories, then restrict to the bounded constructible finite-Tor domain specified in the statement. By [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin](ii), each bounded constructible input admits a bounded constructible etale-origin witness; its shifts do as well. The canonical constant-ring maps are isomorphisms by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map]. Thus [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] identifies geometric pullback with exact termwise inverse image. Its shift comparison is the termwise identity. For every ordinary derived adjunction $Lu^*\dashv Ru_*$, [lem-weil-pbc-derived-adjunction-shift] says that the actual unit and counit commute with these canonical integer shifts; in particular this identifies the shift on $Ru_*$ with the adjunction-compatible one required below. The pullback compositor of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] is termwise on K-flat models. Its component on $P[m]$ in degree $r$ is its component on $P$ in degree $r+m$, so it commutes with every shift, as does the square comparison $\theta$ assembled from it and its inverse.

For any ordinary square, [def-exchange-projection] writes $\operatorname{Ex}_*$ as the composite $\eta_{f'}$, $Rf'_*(\theta)$ and $Rf'_*Lg'^*(\varepsilon_f)$ with the indicated whiskerings. Every factor has the shift equation by step 1. Composition and whiskering preserve that equation by [lem-weil-pbc-commshift-nattrans-comp-whisker]. Applying its four elementary identities to the shift $[m]$ gives the same rule for every fixed integer $m$; equivalently substitute $[m]$ for $[1]$ in its displayed equations. Consequently the ordinary exchange used for $p$ commutes with all integer shifts. This checks the specified mate, not an arbitrary isomorphism of its source and target.

source.place: Tag 014V (definition-exact-functor-triangulated-categories), Tag 014Y (lemma-composition-exact); unit-square-counit formula of def-exchange-projection

proof.text: The open base-change factor $\beta:L\bar g'^*j_!\to j'_!Lg'^*$ is the complex-level canonical comparison of [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change]. Here $j_!$ is exact and degreewise by [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero], and both pullbacks are degreewise by step 1. In degree $r$ at $K[m]$, its component is $\beta_{K^{r+m}}$; the differentials on both sides are multiplied by the same $(-1)^m$. Hence its shift square is equality of these chain maps. The formula of [def-exchange-projection] is $\operatorname{Ex}_!^c=Rp'_*(\beta)\circ\operatorname{Ex}_{*,p}(j_!-)$. Step 2 and the composition/whiskering rule now give the exchange shift equation for these two compactification candidates.

source.place: Open-extension base-change factor in the compactification formula; degreewise calculation

proof.text: For the ordinary projection $\pi_{p;M,L}$ of [def-exchange-projection], [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] supplies the shift equation in $L$, including the canonical tensor-pullback and adjunction structures. [lem-sfb-ringed-projection-first-shift] supplies it in $M$. The hypotheses are met by the constant-$A$ ringed pro-etale topoi, small relative to the module universe; step 1 identifies their canonical direct-image shift with the unique unit/counit-compatible shift used in the latter node. Thus neither invocation changes a shift convention. These two cited equations are for $[1]$; they imply the corresponding equations for all integers by the iteration argument in step 11. Substituting $M=j_!K$ gives the first projection factor with its canonical composite shifts in either $K$ or $L$.

source.place: Tag 0B56 (equation-projection-formula-map), Tag 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product); first-input shift check in lem-sfb-ringed-projection-first-shift

proof.text: Check the open projection factor separately. Represent $L$ by a K-flat complex $P$ with flat terms, using [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. The pullback of $P$ is again K-flat by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Thus the map of [lem-cbc-extension-zero-projection-formula] is computed by the total complex of the canonical sheaf maps $(j_!K^a)\otimes P^b\to j_!(K^a\otimes j^{-1}P^b)$. Exact, degreewise $j_!$ is a left adjoint [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero], so commutes with the direct sums in this total complex. Use the differential $d_K\otimes1+(-1)^a1\otimes d_P$ of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. The comparison $K[m]\otimes P\to(K\otimes P)[m]$ is the identity on each summand; the comparison $K\otimes P[m]\to(K\otimes P)[m]$ is multiplication by $(-1)^{ma}$ on degree-$a$ terms of $K$. The sheaf map above preserves both degrees and is $A$-linear, so commutes with each of these scalars. This proves both shift squares on total models. The same statement holds after derived localization by the cited tensor-descent equivalence; no assertion that geometric stalks detect arbitrary pro-etale morphisms is used.

source.place: Tag 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), total K-flat construction; open-extension projection comparison

proof.text: In $\gamma_{K,L}$ of [def-exchange-projection], the remaining comparison is $Lj^*Lp^*\cong Lf^*$; it commutes with shifts by step 1. Tensoring its components with fixed $K$ commutes with the right-input shifts: on the signed total models of step 5 a degree-zero map preserves the degree $a$, hence the scalar $(-1)^{ma}$. It also respects first-input shifts, whose comparison is the identity on summands. Therefore $\gamma$ has both required shift squares. The chosen-compactification projection is exactly $Rp_*(\gamma)\circ\pi_{p;j_!K,L}$. Steps 4 and 5 and the composite-shift rule [lem-weil-pbc-commshift-nattrans-comp-whisker] give its equation in $K$ and in $L$ (first for $[1]$, and then by step 11 for all integers).

source.place: Tag 0B56 (equation-projection-formula-map), compactification composite specified in def-exchange-projection

proof.text: We must also check the canonical compactification comparisons; naturality alone would not give this. Put $H_T=\nu_T^*$. It is exact termwise comparison pullback by [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact]. The pullback comparison $a_u:H_Uu_e^*\cong u_p^*H_V$ of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] and the sheaf open comparison $e_j:H j^e_!\cong j^p_!H$ of [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison] commute with integer shifts: their degree-$r$ components on a shifted complex are their original degree-$(r+m)$ components. For proper $u$, the specified direct-image comparison $b_u$ is, by [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate], the transpose of $H_U(\varepsilon^e_u)\circ a_u^{-1}$. Explicitly it is $Ru_{p,*}(H_U\varepsilon^e_u\circ a_u^{-1})\circ\eta^p_u H_VRu_{e,*}$. Step 1 applies also to the constant-ring etale adjunctions. Consequently every factor here has the shift square, so $b_u$ does too. Properness supplies the qcqs hypothesis of the named comparison.

source.place: Tags 05SU and 0A8D; canonical counit-mate site comparison

proof.text: For a refinement $u:c_1\to c_2$, its etale proper/open map $\alpha^e_u:j^e_{2!}\to Ru_{e,*}j^e_{1!}$ is the specialization in [lem-cbc-proper-open-interchange-coherence]. On a K-injective representative $J$ it is $j^e_{2!}J\cong u_*j^e_{1!}J\to u_*I$ for a K-injective resolution $j^e_{1!}J\to I$. For the shifted input choose $J[m]$ and the shifted resolution into $I[m]$; both are valid by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-shift]. The proper/open sheaf identification has degree zero; its degree-$r$ component is the original one in degree $r+m$. The resolution arrow also shifts termwise. The displayed representative is consequently exactly the shift of the unshifted representative. Under the canonical resolution identifications this proves the shift square for the named $\alpha^e_u$, for all $m$, and does not assert that $j_!$ preserves K-injectives.

source.place: Tag 0F7B (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open), first paragraph of proof; refinement specialization

proof.text: The pro-etale refinement map has the specified normalization [lem-sf-proper-open-comparison-site-normalization]: $\alpha^p_u e_{j_2}=Ru_{p,*}(e_{j_1})\,b_u j^e_{1!}\,H(\alpha^e_u)$. All factors on the right and $e_{j_2}$ have shift squares by steps 7 and 8; cancel the invertible $e_{j_2}$ to obtain the square for $\alpha^p_u$ on $H_XL$. For a witness $w:H_XL\cong K$, [def-sf-refinement-comparison-isomorphism](a) conjugates this map by $Ru_*j_{1!}(w)$ and $j_{2!}(w)^{-1}$. The shifted witness is $w[m]\chi_H(L)$; naturality of the two composite shift comparisons cancels those witness factors, giving the equation at $K$. For the direct-image compositor in part (b), [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] specifies its representative $v_*t:v_*u_*I\to v_*J$, for a resolution $t:u_*I\to J$. Using $I[m],J[m],t[m]$ proves its shift equation in the same way as step 8. Thus $\theta_u=Rv_*(\alpha_u^{-1})\circ\kappa_{v,u}$ has the canonical shift equation. Inverses are justified by multiplying $\chi_G\tau_{[m]}=\tau[m]\chi_F$ by the two inverses of $\tau$, which yields $\chi_F\tau_{[m]}^{-1}=\tau[m]^{-1}\chi_G$.

source.place: Tag 0F7B; pro-etale normalization and the explicit refinement-comparison formula

proof.text: By [prop-compactification-coherence-detailed], comparisons between any two candidates are composites of refinement maps and their inverses through a common refinement. Step 9 gives the shift equation for all of them. All witnesses remain bounded below after any integer shift; we use comparisons only on that domain. Clause (4) of [fix-lem-exchanges] intertwines the chosen-compactification exchange maps with these comparisons. [fix-prop-projection-formula] supplies the same compatibility for projection. Hence the actual transformations in the statement are obtained from the maps of steps 3 and 6 by pre- and postcomposing these comparison isomorphisms (and tensoring them with the fixed other input for projection). Their shift squares follow by composition; tensoring a degree-zero map preserves the signed comparisons of step 5. This proves the assertions for the named geometric maps, independently of the compactifications.

source.place: Tag 0F7B; compactification coherence and the specified exchange/projection comparison compatibilities

proof.text: For completeness, an equation for $[1]$ between coherent integer-shift functors implies every integer equation. The $m=0$ equation is the original transformation. Paste the squares for $m$ and $1$ and use the coherence $[m][1]\cong[m+1]$ to obtain the square for $m+1$. From the square for $1$ at $M[-1]$, multiply by the invertible shift comparisons and identify $M[-1][1]\cong M$; applying $[-1]$ gives the square for $-1$ at $M$. Repeating gives every negative integer. This applies to the first- and second-variable projection equations used above. Finally, wherever $\tau$ is invertible, the inverse calculation in step 9 gives the same equation with source and target reversed for every $m$.
